newsitem.title: USA: Baxter, Genentech in hemophilia therapy agreement.
newsitem.headline: Baxter, Genentech in hemophilia therapy agreement.

text.p: The Biotech Group of Baxter International Inc's Baxter Healthcare Corp and Genentech Inc said on Tuesday they had signed a collaborative agreement to jointly develop a cellular therapy for hemophilia A.

The collaboration would combine Genentech's scientific skills and intellectual property relating to Factor VIII production in cells and Baxter's proprietary TheraCyte immunoisolation technology, the companies said in a joint news release.

Under the agreement, Genentech will develop an engineered cell line for use in Baxter's TheraCyte system, and Baxter will perform all other preclinical and clinical studies. Genentech also will grant Baxter a worldwide exclusive license to its relevant intellectual property for products developed under the collaboration.

At demonstration of clinical viability in a Phase I trial, which the companies said they expected to conduct in the "next several years," Genentech will have the option to equally share with Baxter in the program's profits and expenses or to accept royalties.
The TheraCyte system is comprised of an implantable device and human allogeneic cells genetically modified to produce a desired protein, in this case Factor VIII.
The companies said the gene therapy, if successful, could eliminate the need for injections to stop severe bleeding during trauma and lower the long-term morbidity of hemophilia.

Hemophilia A is a blood coagulation disorder caused by a genetic deficiency in the body's ability to produce Factor VIII. It affects roughly 40,000 people in North America, Europe and Japan and can cause severe bleeding and joint destruction.
Baxter International is a global medical products and service company. Genentech is a biotechnology company. ((--Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
